messages.author: f6aff3ab0165e685
messages.subject: Themes and fonts
parts:
I am trying to create my own theme by modifying "theme_grey" to use Arial (or any font) and some other things, but I am having some trouble getting it to work.  Below is an example of working code I am basing my approach on followed by my theme and an invocation of that theme that does not work.  The problem appears to stem from   "   text = element_text(size=base_size, family = "Arial"),   " in the first line of replacements.  It give the following error message:  "Error in FUN("text"[[1L]], ...) : Theme element 'text' has NULL property: face, colour, size, hjust, vjust, angle, lineheight"  My understanding from the wiki is that if I set "text," all subsequent text elements will inherit those properties?

What am I doing wrong?

#######################################################
library(ggplot)

##load Arial font for use below
install.packages("extrafont")
library(extrafont)
font_import(pattern="[A/a]rial")
loadfonts(device="win")

#example that works
x11()
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + 
  geom_point() +
  theme(text=element_text(size=12, family="Arial"))

##Now, set up my own theme by modifying theme_grey

theme_ch1<-function (base_size = 12, base_family = "") 
{
  theme_grey(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace% 
    theme(text = element_text(size=base_size, family = "Arial"),  #this is the offending bit of code
          axis.text  = element_text(size = rel(0.8)), 
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"), 
          legend.key = element_rect(colour = "grey80"), 
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white",colour = NA), 
          panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey50"), 
          panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA), 
          panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA), 
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"), 
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"))
}

x11()
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + 
  geom_point() +
  theme_ch1()
###############################################################


Thanks,

Thomas

parts: Hi:

On Tue, Mar 26, 2013 at 4:16 PM, Thomas <thoma...@maine.edu> wrote:
> I am trying to create my own theme by modifying "theme_grey" to use Arial
> (or any font) and some other things, but I am having some trouble getting it
> to work. Below is an example of working code I am basing my approach on
> followed by my theme and an invocation of that theme that does not work.
> The problem appears to stem from " text = element_text(size=base_size,
> family = "Arial"), " in the first line of replacements. It give the
> following error message: "Error in FUN("text"[[1L]], ...) : Theme element
> 'text' has NULL property: face, colour, size, hjust, vjust, angle,
> lineheight" My understanding from the wiki is that if I set "text," all
> subsequent text elements will inherit those properties?
>
> What am I doing wrong?
>
> #######################################################
> library(ggplot)
Does this actually work???? :)

>
> ##load Arial font for use below
> install.packages("extrafont")
> library(extrafont)
> font_import(pattern="[A/a]rial")
> loadfonts(device="win")
>
> #example that works
> x11()
> ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
> geom_point() +
> theme(text=element_text(size=12, family="Arial"))
>
> ##Now, set up my own theme by modifying theme_grey
>
> theme_ch1<-function (base_size = 12, base_family = "")
> {
> theme_grey(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%
> theme(text = element_text(size=base_size, family = "Arial"), #this is
> the offending bit of code
> axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
> axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
> legend.key = element_rect(colour = "grey80"),
> panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white",colour = NA),
> panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey50"),
> panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
> panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
> strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour =
> "grey50"),
> strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour =
> "grey50"))
> }
Here's what I get when trying to run the code below:
Error in FUN("text"[[1L]], ...) :

Theme element 'text' has NULL property: face, colour, hjust, vjust,
angle, lineheight

and this is correct.

This will be a little long, so strap in :)

Let's start here:

> theme_ch1()
List of 38
$ line :List of 4
..$ colour : chr "black"
..$ size : num 0.5
..$ linetype: num 1
..$ lineend : chr "butt"
..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element_line" "element"
$ rect :List of 4
..$ fill : chr "white"
..$ colour : chr "black"
..$ size : num 0.5
..$ linetype: num 1
..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element_rect" "element"
$ text :List of 8
..$ family : chr "Arial"
..$ face : NULL
..$ colour : NULL
..$ size : num 12
..$ hjust : NULL
..$ vjust : NULL
..$ angle : NULL
..$ lineheight: NULL
..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element_text" "element"
<snip>

These are the values associated with the top tier elements in your
theme function. Notice that all of the list components under $line and
$rect are non-NULL - so should all of the list components in
theme_ch1$text. The reason this happened is because %+replace% wiped
out the previous contents and replaced them with NULL except for the
elements you specified. Contrast the following toy examples:

# Modify an element of theme_grey():
mytheme1 <- theme_grey() + theme(text = element_text(colour="red"))
mytheme1$text
# List of 8
# $ family : chr "Helvetica"
# $ face : chr "plain"
# $ colour : chr "red"
# $ size : num 12
# $ hjust : num 0.5
# $ vjust : num 0.5
# $ angle : num 0
# $ lineheight: num 0.9
# - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

# Replace it instead:
mytheme2 <- theme_grey() %+replace% theme(text = element_text(colour="red"))
mytheme2$text
# List of 8
# $ family : NULL
# $ face : NULL
# $ colour : chr "red"
# $ size : NULL
# $ hjust : NULL
# $ vjust : NULL
# $ angle : NULL
# $ lineheight: NULL
# - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

This is the danger of replacing theme elements at the top of the
hierarchy. Typically, it's easier to replace theme elements further
down the tree; most of the values beyond the top tier are NULL because
they inherit their values from the top tier elements (text, line,
rect). To do this right, you need to restate the default values in the
top element text:

theme_ch1<-function (base_size = 12, base_family = "")
{
theme_grey(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%

theme(text = element_text(size = base_size, family = "Arial", face
= "plain",
colour = "black", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5,
angle = 0, lineheight = 0.9),

axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
legend.key = element_rect(colour = "grey80"),
panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white",colour = NA),
panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey50"),
panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"),
strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"))
}
# and now the plot works...

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
geom_point() +
theme_ch1()

Another alternative would be to skip the replacement of text in the
theme and add it as a modifier in the plot function call:

theme_ch1a <-function (base_size = 12, base_family = "")

{
theme_grey(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%
theme( axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),

axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
legend.key = element_rect(colour = "grey80"),
panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white",colour = NA),
panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey50"),
panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA, size = NA),
strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"),
strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey80", colour = "grey50"))
}

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
geom_point() +

theme_ch1a() + theme(text = element_text(family = "Arial"))


Dennis
